newsitem.title: USA: Alex Penelas elected mayor of Dade County, Fla..
newsitem.headline: Alex Penelas elected mayor of Dade County, Fla..

text.p: Dade County Commissioner Alex Penelas was elected mayor of the county after garnering 60 percent of the vote, elections officials said.
Penelas defeated former County Commission President Arthur Teele in Tuesday's nonpartisan run-off election.
Penelas, 34, is the first to hold the post since voters approved the strong mayor form of government and will draft the county's $4 billion budget and choose a county manager and commission chairman.
He said he would keep Armando Vidal as county manager and appoint Commissioner Gwen Margolis as commission chairman.
Penelas is a Democrat, a former lawyer, former U.S. Army Ranger and served as mass transit chief under President Reagan.

In county commission races, lawyer Jimmy Morales defeated carpet supply executive Mavel Cruz for the District 7 seat. Commissioner Maurice Ferre had held that seat but resigned to run for mayor. He lost to Penelas and Teele in the Sept 3 election.
Commissioner Dennis Moss easily won re-election to the District 9 seat, defeating lawyer Henry Marinello.
Former Commissioner Barbara Carey defeated Billy Hardemon in the race for the District 3 commission seat, which Teele gave up to make his mayoral bid.

Hardemon was chief of staff for County Commissioner James Burke before entering the commission race. The Miami Herald has reported that federal prosecutors are targeting him an Burke ine a probe of alleged kickbacks involving county bond deals. Both denied wrongdoing and neither has been charged.
